intro: Lynn is next door to Saugus. Shane has repaired a combi boiler in Lynn and done maintenance plumbing for a new homeowner there. Both jobs are below, with photos.

local_hooks.h: A combi boiler that would not heat the house
local_hooks.b: On a Navien combi boiler a failed three-way diverter valve could not send water to space heat. The call for heat kept running through the hot water heat exchanger, and the boiler's internal circulator pump wore out. Both parts were replaced under warranty, and the customer had heat and hot water again.

For a customer who had just bought a house in Lynn, Shane added a shut-off with a drain on the house side of the water meter, with adapters for the fine-thread brass water main, for emergencies. He also cut out corroding SharkBite fittings and repiped with press fittings.

local_hooks.h: A cold shower, then 2 inches of water in the basement
local_hooks.b: A shower turned cold, and the customer found about 2 inches of water in the basement. The emergency shut-off valve on the heater did not work, so the water to the whole house had to be shut off. Shane replaced the heater and the customer had hot water back.

intro: Shane remodeled a half bathroom and added a coffee wash-down area in a Lexington therapy office for its new owner (shared February 2026). The building's rules shaped how the hot water was set up.

local_hooks.b: The building only allows point-of-use water heaters. Shane gave each fixture a 1.0 GPM flow device, fed through a Sloan point-of-use compression mixing valve.

local_hooks.h: Why the mixing valve is there
local_hooks.b: With the mixing valve in the line, the heaters can be set to their maximum temperature. That gives the most hot water at each fixture.
